subject: Sandbox on‑prem: pod network segmentation & PVC strategy
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgelabs.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sandbox on-prem: initial constraints and ask

Hi Rishi / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've started a small internal sandbox to validate performance and operational patterns before committing to a Dedicated contract. A few constraints up front so we focus the review:

- Two racks at our London DC, each with 4x 8‑GPU nodes (A100-style), separate top-of-rack switches.
- Storage: vendor-provided SAN (iSCSI LUNs) + two hosts with local NVMe for caching. No clustered filesystem allowed in prod for now.
- Networking: existing leaf-spine, MTU 9000 on the fabric. Internal security wants strict pod segmentation between tenant workloads and infra (control-plane, model-serving).
- Backups: snapshots must be possible for model checkpoints; we prefer CSI snapshots.

Top asks: can Redwood's Private runtime be deployed in this topology with:
1) predictable low-latency KV cache for LLMs (use local NVMe?),
2) safe PVC reclaim / snapshot policy for checkpoints,
3) network policy recommendations to ensure tenant isolation + cross-node inference traffic performance.

I've attached a short constraints PDF and a draft PVC mapping sheet. Would you and Dev be available for a focused architecture call tomorrow?

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Ops Lead, EdgeLabs Solutions
liam@edgelabs.com

Attachments: edgelabs-onprem-constraints.pdf, proposed-pvc-mapping.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sandbox on-prem: initial constraints and ask

Thanks Liam — good summary. Quick answers up front and then a proposal for the call agenda: 

Short answers:
- Local NVMe for KV cache: yes — recommend using emptyDir:SizeLimit backed by local NVMe for cache hot path and configure read‑through caching to persistent PVCs. Avoid using hostPath for portability.
- PVC snapshots: CSI snapshot support is the right call; we'll validate your SAN driver's snapshot compatibility. If not supported, we can use periodic application-level checkpointing to object storage via an agent.
- Pod segmentation: use a combination of CNI (Calico with policy enforcement) + dedicated node pools for infra vs tenant workloads + strict taints/tolerations. For east-west MTU-sensitive traffic we'll validate MTU alignment across host, CNI, and iSCSI path.

Proposed 45min call agenda (tomorrow 13:00 UTC):
1) Run through your attachment constraints (5m)
2) Nodepool mapping: which roles get local NVMe, which use SAN-backed PVCs (10m)
3) Network layout: MTU, BGP peering needs, CNI choice and policy (15m)
4) Snapshot / backup approach and retention (10m)

Action: Marissa / Dev / Soojin — can you join? Dev, please prepare a quick slide on recommended storage classes and reclaim policies. Soojin, please pull any prior MTU troubleshooting notes.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi all —

High-level storage proposal notes (attaching a simple mapping sheet):

- Node roles and PV types:
  * model-worker (8 GPUs): local NVMe for KV cache (emptyDir with device-level isolation), SAN LUNs for long-term checkpoints mounted as ReadWriteOnce PVCs.
  * infra (ingress, metrics, control-plane proxies): SAN-backed PVCs.
  * batch/ingest: SAN-backed, high replication.

- PVC reclaim policy: set Retain for checkpoint PVCs by default (so customer retains volumes after pod deletion) + lifecycle hook to transfer to object store on cleanup. Dev recommends a custom reclaim-controller to automate archival.

- Snapshot cadence: hourly lightweight CSI snapshots for smaller checkpoint deltas, daily full offload to object store. We'll validate snapshot sizes against SAN throughput.

- Block device plan for LMDB/rocksdb: prefer raw block PVCs via CSI to avoid filesystem overhead for memmapped DBs.

I'll bring the proposed storageclass YAML + example reclaim-controller in the call.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding network considerations from our side:

- CNI choice: Calico in policy-only mode is fine, but for performance-sensitive east-west we prefer Cilium with eBPF for lower kernel hops and better load balancing. If you need L7 policies and Envoy‑style sidecars, Calico+Istio is an option but increases latency.
- MTU: Confirm all hosts, ToR, and SAN iSCSI path are set to 9000. iSCSI encapsulation can reduce effective MTU — run an MTU path validation before large model checkpoints are transferred.
- Nodepool sizing: make a small GPU worker pool (3 nodes) with local NVMe for caching and a slightly larger non-GPU pool for infra + retries to keep control-plane traffic off GPU nodes.
- Service mesh: avoid injecting sidecars into model worker pods by using node selectors and a dedicated ingress for model requests; use hostNetwork=true for grpc heavy workloads only if you can accept reduced isolation.

I'll include a short MTU-checklist and a recommended Calico/Cilium matrix on the call.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — the agenda works. Quick follow ups before the call: 

1) We cannot change the SAN vendor, so any CSI behaviour dependency needs to be mapped. I'll send the SAN driver contact and admin access for a CSI test cluster.
2) For the local NVMe approach: we prefer the cache to survive pod restarts on the same node (warm cache). Is there a recommended pattern to persist cache across pod restarts but not across full node reprovision?
3) What's the recommended approach for cross-node KV replication (async vs shared backend)? Lower latency is important for single‑request QPS > 500.

I'll add the SAN driver contact in a follow-up and will upload MTU test captures. See you on the call.

—Liam
